judgment.notes: M004: X=ℝ, G=measures on its Borel space, μ=λ, K=ℕ, T_i=J_i. D008 gives a measure and thus the required FunLike/OuterMeasureClass structures; the family is countable. M005 at endpoints 0,1 gives λ(I)=1. M006 applies to each explicitly constructed open interval with finite ordered endpoints; its endpoint difference is its nonnegative length, bounded by F002. Empty J_i contribute zero (also M006 with equal endpoints). BG009 checks the omitted monotonicity step. E001 uses A=I with a>1 in S001 and 0<s<1 in S004, then A=F⊆Eucl(n+1), 0<v<1 in S005. D003 is exactly the diameter-cover normalization in E001; no measurability, compactness or positive ambient-dimension premise is introduced. The displayed earlier measure conclusions supply the antecedents of its converse implications.

S001's equal pieces cover [0,1], and for each fixed scale and tolerance one sufficiently large N makes both mesh and a-cost small (BG001–BG006). S002's finite diameters bound each nonempty W_i, so its explicitly enlarged endpoints give covering open intervals of the asserted lengths (BG007–BG008). S003 uses countable subadditivity only after enlargement, obtains ∑ρ_i≥1 without assuming summability, and uses the correctly reversed negative-exponent inequality; zero diameters and infinite sums are handled (BG009–BG013, BG016–BG017). S004's power bound is unbounded as δ↓0 with s fixed (BG014), giving infinite measure and the lower dimension bound, not an unjustified limit exchange. S005 pulls every F-cover back along a genuine isometric vertical copy, compares positive powers (BG015), then takes infima and suprema in the correct directions. Dimension bounds for every 0<v<1 imply ≥1 also if dimension is infinite. The argument includes n=0 and the D=0 implication.

Each declared premise has a real use: H001 provides the vertical-copy point; M004 supplies subadditivity; M005 normalizes the unit interval; M006 evaluates the enclosing open intervals; E001 converts zero/infinite measures to the three dimension bounds. Seventeen recorded background notes transparently account for routine real powers and their limits, real interval diameter/extrema bounds, measure monotonicity, geometric errors and nonnegative sums. The core interval lower-bound and pullback-cover arguments are actually displayed, not imported as dimension monotonicity or a project result. No use of a claimed enlarged calculation policy was needed.

F001 is established before S004; F002 is constructed under L1–L3 before J is chosen; F003 universally closes W and no longer depends on ε; F004 exports both dim_H I=1 and the full quantified infinite-measure fact needed by S005. S005 proves the cover pullback comparison locally using D001/D002/D003, rather than borrowing an ancestor's isometry theorem. All remaining factual uses are conditional direct inputs, these prior local conclusions, consequences of the supplied infimum/supremum definitions, finite order/algebra, or the 17 positively checked recorded notes. No absent N, hidden original H, or source proof is used.

The conditional premises are exactly H001, M004, M005, M006 and E001. H001 supplies x0∈E; the three M statements are used for Lebesgue measure on ℝ and countable interval families, and E001 is instantiated only at positive exponents on the specified Euclidean sets. No input N or producer body is assumed. Source authenticity is outside this conditional review.

Global occurrences of Eucl, diam, H, dim_H, I, F, D and λ have their typed D001–D008 meanings, with n,E ambient parameters and no hidden condition on D. In S001 N is the positive-integer piece count and limit index, and a is quantified with a>1. Sequence indices i are bound by the sequence formulas and sums. S002 introduces real s,δ,ε, W_i⊆ℝ and finite real ρ_i; boundedness and enclosure justify the infimum/supremum endpoints (BG007–BG008). Interval length here is the difference of these explicitly displayed endpoints. F002 supplies J before its choice. In S005 H001 supplies x0∈Eucl(n); v,d and the Eucl(n+1) cover V are locally arbitrary, and T_i is explicitly defined as a subset of I. The distance identity uses locally quantified t,u∈I. No chosen point, interval family or cover is exported as a free global object.
